title: fix(adapter-utils): make the managed git launcher work on Windows
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - Agents do real work in a repository, so Paperclip stages a managed `git` and `gh` launcher next to each run and puts that directory first on PATH
> - The launcher builds the run PATH, and the shim resolves the real `git` binary from the inherited PATH
> - Both steps assume POSIX, so on Windows the PATH is joined with the wrong character and the binary lookup ignores PATHEXT
> - Every managed git and gh call in an agent run then fails on Windows, with an error that points nowhere near the cause
> - This pull request corrects the PATH join and makes the binary lookup PATHEXT aware
> - The benefit is that agent runs on Windows can use git again, and the POSIX behaviour does not change

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #14091

I searched open and closed pull requests for `PATHEXT`, `path.delimiter`, `github-launcher` and `execution-target`. I found no duplicate and no in-flight work.

**What happened:** The managed git launcher does not work on Windows. Two defects cause this.

1. `packages/adapter-utils/src/execution-target.ts` joined the launcher directory to the inherited PATH with a hardcoded `:`. Windows delimits PATH with `;`. The join makes the launcher directory and the first inherited element into one invalid element. The value goes to the run PATH and to six profile files.
2. `packages/adapter-utils/src/github-launcher.ts` probed only `path.join(directory, program)`. Windows resolves a bare `git` through PATHEXT and carries `git.exe` on disk. The extensionless name does not exist, so the lookup returns `undefined` and the shim exits 127.

**Expected behavior:** `git --version` through the managed launcher exits 0 on Windows.

**Steps to reproduce:** Run an agent on Windows. Run any git command. The command fails. The reporter of #14091 verified both defects against a live PowerShell environment.

**Paperclip version:** `2026.916.1`. Both defects are present on `master` at `d3e0f0a`.

**Deployment mode:** Self-hosted server.

**Agent adapters involved:** All adapters that use the managed git launcher.

## What Changed

- `execution-target.ts`: the local branch now joins PATH with `path.delimiter`. The remote branch keeps `:`.
- `github-launcher.ts`: the executable lookup now probes the PATHEXT-qualified candidates before the extensionless name.
- `github-launcher.test.ts`: two cases, plus a shared fixture.

**One deviation from the issue.** #14091 proposes `path.delimiter` for the PATH join without a condition. That change would introduce a different defect. `githubOperationLauncherBasePath` returns the remote shell's own PATH for a remote target. It reads it over `sh`, and `prepareGitHubOperationLaunchers` writes it into POSIX profiles on the remote host as `export PATH=...`. That value is always `:`-delimited, whatever the controller runs. An unconditional `path.delimiter` makes a Windows controller write `;` into a remote POSIX profile and breaks a path that works today. The fix therefore uses `remote ? ":" : path.delimiter`.

## Verification

The fixture stages the shim in one directory and puts a second directory on PATH that holds only a node symlink. A real system `bin` directory would supply a genuine extensionless `git`, which is the candidate the case must not find.

Red, with the source change reverted and the tests kept:

```
 × resolves a PATHEXT-qualified executable when the extensionless name is absent
   Error: Command failed: /tmp/paperclip-github-pathext-uO4nBA/managed/git --version
   Paperclip: requested GitHub command is not installed.

 Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 7 skipped (9)
```

The failure is the shim's own not-found guard, which is the symptom #14091 reports.

Green, after the change:

```
$ node_modules/.bin/vitest run packages/adapter-utils
 Test Files  60 passed (60)
      Tests  1293 passed | 5 skipped (1298)

$ pnpm --filter @paperclipai/adapter-utils typecheck
(clean)
```

`master` gives `1291 passed` for the same package, and the two added cases account for the difference.

**What I did not verify.** I have no Windows machine. Both cases run on Linux, and the PATHEXT case exercises the real lookup because PATHEXT drives it on any platform. The PATH delimiter change is different: `path.delimiter` is `:` on Linux, so a Linux runner cannot observe the Windows value. That half rests on `path.delimiter` semantics and on the reporter's PowerShell evidence, not on a test run here.

#14091 also asks for a Windows CI leg for this package. I did not add one, because I cannot confirm that it passes before I push it. It is worth a separate pull request.

One unrelated note: `http2-bridge-server.test.ts` emitted one unhandled `NGHTTP2_REFUSED_STREAM` teardown error during a full parallel run. It does not reproduce when that file runs alone, on `master` or on this branch.

## Risks

Low risk on POSIX. PATHEXT is unset there, so the candidate list collapses to the single extensionless entry that the lookup has always probed. The `keeps resolving the extensionless program when PATHEXT is unset` case pins that behaviour.

The remote path is unchanged by design, so SSH and sandbox runs keep the delimiter they use today.

A POSIX host that sets PATHEXT would probe extra candidates before the extensionless name. This is very rare, and the extra candidates almost never exist.

## Model Used

Claude Opus 5 (1M context), model ID `claude-opus-5`, provided by Anthropic and run through Claude Code. Extended reasoning was on. The model used tool access to read the repository, run vitest and tsc, and inspect the results.

title: fix(issues): let an agent name a cross-agent unblock owner, and keep the handing-off run bound
body:
Found while dispositioning TES-151.

## The defect

Every write to `unblockDescriptor.owner` by an agent was refused with `{"error":"Agents may only name themselves as an unblock owner"}`. All three non-self owner forms — `{agentId: <other agent>}`, `"board"`, and `{userId: "local-board"}` — were unreachable.

The field exists to say *who unblocks this and what they must do*, but by construction it could only ever say *I unblock this*, which is the one case that carries no information: a self-named owner on a self-assigned issue is already visible from `assigneeAgentId`.

Seven issues were `blocked` on another agent's action and could not record it through this field: TES-42, TES-56, TES-75, TES-96, TES-106, TES-122, TES-124. The information existed only in prose comments where nothing enforced it.

## The fix

The self-only restriction is replaced by the check that actually mattered: **the write must be attributable to a run bound to *this* issue.**

Naming a blocker does not hijack another agent's queue. `blockedByIssueIds` and `assigneeAgentId` own routing; `unblockDescriptor` is descriptive. So an agent that is a live run for this issue can name any valid owner.

The company-boundary check (`Unblock owner agent must belong to the issue company`) and the active-membership check (`Unblock owner user must be an active company member`) are unchanged and still apply to every owner form, including self-naming. **This widens who may be named and never what may be named.**

Self-naming is left working with no run binding at all, since it was never the case the restriction was really about.

The refusal is now 422 with the reason rather than a bare 403.

## The disposition side

The same defect, seen from the other end. The status PATCH that set `blocked` cleared `checkoutRunId`, and a `blocked` issue refuses checkout outright (`Issue is blocked by unresolved blockers`). So the binding could never be re-acquired, and an agent that legitimately finished work and blocked it on someone else lost the ability to record why — in any field.

The run already holding the checkout now keeps it across the transition into `blocked`. Bounds on that carve-out:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| the run holding the checkout sets `blocked` | keeps the lock |
| a different run sets `blocked` | releases, as before |
| a board write with no run sets `blocked` | releases, as before |
| any other non-`in_progress` status | releases, as before |
| the run later goes terminal | `clearCheckoutRunIfTerminal` reclaims it |

So a blocked issue cannot pin a lock open indefinitely, and no other path is widened.

## Verification

464 tests pass across the affected suites (issue routes, issues service against embedded postgres, blocker attention and diagnostics, stale-lock routes and sweep, cross-issue influence, execution policy, comment attribution, assignee invokability, shared validators).

`tsc --noEmit` reports 116 errors on this branch and 116 on `origin/master` — all pre-existing, from an unvendored `@paperclipai/paperclip-runner`. None are in the files this touches.

The new tests were checked against the unfixed source, so they are not self-confirming:

- **7 route tests and 2 service tests** that assert the new behaviour fail without the source change.
- The **negative controls** — different-issue run, run belonging to another agent, different-run block, board block, terminal-status block, out-of-company owner, non-member user — pass either way, which is what makes them controls.

## Note on scope

The OpenAPI description for `unblockDescriptor` was not changed. It does not state the self-only rule, so it remains accurate.

Base is `d3e0f0a2` (`master` at time of opening).

title: fix(cli): stop running npm against pnpm, Yarn, and Bun global installs
body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work
> - Operators install the `paperclipai` CLI and use `paperclipai update` to move to a new release
> - The CLI supports a global install, and the bug-report template lists "npm / pnpm global install" as one method
> - `detectInstallMode` marks every path that contains `/node_modules/paperclipai/` as `global-npm`
> - pnpm, Yarn, and Bun global installs also contain that path segment, so `update` runs `npm install -g` against an install that npm does not own
> - The npm command then fails, or it prints "Updated" and the running service keeps the old code
> - This pull request detects pnpm, Yarn, and Bun global installs and shows the correct command for that package manager instead of running npm
> - The benefit is that `update` does not report a false success on a global install that npm does not own

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Fixes #13861

Related:
- Refs #11795. That PR also changes `cli/src/commands/update.ts` (release channels). It does not change install-mode detection. The two PRs can conflict in the same file.
- Refs #11755. That issue is about a different false-positive in `doctor` for global npm installs.

## What Changed

- `cli/src/commands/update.ts`: `detectInstallMode` now finds three more modes before it uses the `global-npm` fallback:
  - `global-pnpm`: the path contains `/pnpm/global/`, or the path is inside `$PNPM_HOME`.
  - `global-yarn`: the path contains `/yarn/global/` or `/Yarn/Data/global/` (Windows).
  - `global-bun`: the path contains `/.bun/install/global/`.
- `detectInstallMode` resolves the real path of the executable before it classifies the install. npm, Yarn, and Bun link bin entries as symlinks, and Node does not resolve `process.argv[1]`. The managed-install check still runs first on the unresolved path.
- For global installs, `update --check` reports the version of the running CLI. Before this change, a managed-install manifest on the same host replaced that version.
- The Node version check does not run for pnpm, Yarn, and Bun global installs, because `update` only prints a command for them.
- `detectInstallMode` accepts an optional `env` argument, so tests can set `PNPM_HOME`. The default is `process.env`.
- `paperclipai update --check` works for the three new modes. It reports the current version, the target version, and if an update is available.
- `paperclipai update` does not run npm for the three new modes. It shows the correct command for that package manager (`action: "manual"`), and tells the operator to restart the running service. Example for pnpm: `pnpm add -g paperclipai@<version> --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org`.
- `doc/INSTALLING.md`: one added sentence about this behavior.
- `cli/src/__tests__/update-command.test.ts`: new tests for detection, detection through a linked bin entry, the `update` flow for all three managers, unsupported Node, and a managed manifest next to a global install. The link test uses a directory junction, so it also runs on Windows without Developer Mode.

The issue also reports that the `global-npm` path does not take a pre-update backup and does not restart the service. This PR does not change that. It is a separate change, and I can open a follow-up PR.

## Verification

- Run `pnpm --filter paperclipai exec vitest run src/__tests__/update-command.test.ts`.
- These new tests pass:
  - `detects pnpm, yarn, and bun global installs instead of reporting them as npm`
  - `detects a yarn / bun global install launched through its symlinked bin entry`
  - `prints the owning manager's command for a global-pnpm / global-yarn / global-bun install and never runs npm install`
  - `prints the pnpm command on unsupported Node because it installs nothing`
  - `reports update availability for a pnpm global install from the running version, not a managed manifest`
- The existing `global-npm` tests pass without changes. This includes the registry isolation test and the downgrade confirmation test.
- Manual check with a pnpm global install:
  1. Run `pnpm add -g paperclipai`.
  2. Run `paperclipai update --check --json`. The result shows `"mode": "global-pnpm"`.
  3. Run `paperclipai update --json`. The result shows `"action": "manual"` and a `pnpm add -g ...` command. npm does not run.
- I ran the tests on Windows 11 without Developer Mode. On that host, 13 existing tests in this file fail with `EPERM` because `fs.symlinkSync` needs Developer Mode. The same 13 tests fail on `master` without this change. They do not come from this change. CI on Linux runs them.
- `tsc --noEmit` for the `cli` package shows no errors in `cli/src`.

## Risks

- Low risk. The change adds modes. It does not change the npm, managed, npx, or source paths.
- For pnpm, Yarn, and Bun global installs, `update` now shows a command and does not install. Before this change, it ran npm, which failed or did not change the install that runs. Scripts that parse `--json` output get a new `mode` value and `action: "manual"`.
- Real-path resolution also changes detection for global npm installs that start through a linked bin (for example `/usr/local/bin/paperclipai`). Before this change, such a start did not match `/node_modules/paperclipai/`. Now it resolves to `global-npm`, as the mode name intends.
- A custom global folder that does not match these patterns and is not inside `$PNPM_HOME` still resolves to `global-npm`. That is the same as the current behavior.
- If #11795 merges first, this PR needs a rebase in `update.ts`.

> For core feature work, check [`ROADMAP.md`](ROADMAP.md) first and discuss it in `#dev` before opening the PR. Feature PRs that overlap with planned core work may need to be redirected — check the roadmap first. See `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Model Used

- Provider: Anthropic
- Model: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), used through Claude Code (CLI agent)
- Capabilities used: tool use (file read/edit, shell, `gh` CLI), code execution for local tests
- The model helped with issue triage, the implementation, the tests, and this description. A human reviewed the change and approved it.

title: fix(dev): load the repo-root .env into the dev server process (#13816)
body:
<!-- Write all pull request text in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100): short sentences, one instruction per step, simple approved vocabulary, and the active voice. -->

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is the open source app people use to manage AI agents for work.
> - `claude_local` runs get their issue-write credential (`PAPERCLIP_API_KEY`) from a local agent JWT. The server signs that JWT with `PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET` / `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`.
> - The issue's reproduction starts the server with `pnpm dev:once`. That runs `scripts/dev-runner.{ts,mjs}` with the server's cwd set to `server/`.
> - The server loads only two env files: the instance file (`~/.paperclip/instances/default/.env`) and a `.env` inside its own cwd. A repo-root `.env` is never loaded, even though the runner watches it for restarts.
> - Result: a developer who sets `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` in the repo-root `.env` gets a server with no agent JWT secret. Every run silently starts without `PAPERCLIP_API_KEY`; agents can comment but cannot set a disposition, and the platform blames the agent (#13816).
> - The fix belongs in the dev runner: it already builds the exact env object it passes to the spawned server, and it is the component that knows the repo root.
> - This pull request loads the repo-root `.env` into that env object with set-if-absent precedence, in both runner variants, and logs which keys it applied.
> - The benefit is that a working local setup no longer loses the secret depending on which directory the server starts in.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

- Refs: #13816

This PR implements the second part of the issue's "Expected" list (load the repo-root `.env` so a local setup does not lose the secret). The first part (board-level visibility / not blaming the agent) is a separate UI and run-outcome change; I plan a follow-up for it if maintainers want it in this shape. Claim comment: https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/issues/13816#issuecomment-5846234829

## What Changed

- `scripts/dev-runner-env-file.mjs` (new): a dotenv-format parser (comments, `export` prefix, single/double quotes, `\n` escapes) and a set-if-absent merge. A real shell export and the instance env file keep precedence, matching dotenv's own no-override behavior.
- `scripts/dev-runner.ts` and `scripts/dev-runner.mjs`: apply the repo-root `.env` to the env object that is passed to the spawned server process, and print one line naming the keys that were applied.
- `server/src/__tests__/dev-runner-repo-env.test.ts` (new): parse rules, precedence, loader behavior against a temp repo root, and missing-file no-op.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run server/src/__tests__/dev-runner-repo-env.test.ts server/src/__tests__/dev-runner-snapshot.test.ts server/src/__tests__/dev-runner-output.test.ts server/src/__tests__/dev-runner-worktree.test.ts` → 18 passed.
- Manual reproduction of the issue's step 1–3, from the real runner with a stub `pnpm`:
  - `node scripts/dev-runner.mjs dev` with `SLOT8_PROBE=hello-from-root` in the repo-root `.env` prints `[paperclip] loaded repo-root .env into the server process: SLOT8_PROBE`.
  - `npx tsx ../scripts/dev-runner.ts dev` from the `server/` cwd prints the same line.
  - Mutation check: with the two runner edits stashed, the same command prints zero loader lines (reproduces the silent gap). With them restored, the line returns.
- The instance env file and `server/.env` keep precedence because the merge only fills keys that are not already set, and the server's own dotenv loads are no-override.

## Risks

- Behavioral shift for source-checkout developers only: values in the repo-root `.env` now reach the dev server process when they are not already set. This is the requested behavior in #13816.
- No production/deployed surface changes. `dev-runner` is not used by Docker or managed installs.
- The parser supports the common dotenv forms, not multi-line values. Those keys are ignored, the same as today's no-op behavior.

## Model Used

- Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context, extended thinking) via Qoder
